cover.headline: A shock-absorber maker turned group holding vehicle: the deals add earnings, and the price already counts them
cover.lead: Gabriel India makes shock absorbers and struts for two-wheelers, cars and trucks (FY26 restated revenue ₹5,245 cr). Since mid-2025 the Anand Group has made it its listed consolidation vehicle: a scheme (effective May-2026) brought in Anchemco's fluids and stakes in Dana Anand and Henkel Anand, and in Sep-2026 Gabriel bought 28.99% of HL Mando Anand from its promoter and ~30% of HL Klemove India, paid with 1.44 cr new shares, ₹350 cr of cash and ₹1,000 cr of NCDs. We forecast EPS of ₹27.3 / ₹34.3 / ₹39.4 for FY27-29E on today's 19.16 cr shares, below the street's ~₹35-41 for FY28E, with ~46% of FY28E profit before tax coming from JVs and associates (30% in restated FY26). The street values Gabriel on **P/E on FY28E EPS** (Motilal Oswal and ICICI Securities ~40x, Choice 32x). The house multiple, its 38.1x forward-P/E median since the scheme was announced (Jul-2025) cut by the 8.6% auto-component move over the same window, is **35x Sep-28E EPS of ₹36.8 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,100, DCF ₹560 (both value the JV stakes only at book). Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A solid ride-control franchise with little pricing power
arguments.p: Market leader in CV shock absorbers (88%) and electric two-wheelers (~60%), 32% of 2W/3W and 25% of cars (company, FY26); revenue ~₹4,600 cr standalone. But EBITDA margins have stayed at 6-10% for two decades, commodity costs are passed on late (Q1FY27 standalone margin 8.4%), and it lost car share in Q1FY27 on model mix.

arguments.h: The deals buy good businesses, paid partly in expensive paper
arguments.p: Dana Anand (ROE 33%), Henkel Anand (62%) and HL Mando Anand (FY26 PAT ₹358 cr) are better businesses than Gabriel's own. HL Mando Anand came at 21.5x earnings, largely in Gabriel shares at ~54x restated FY26 EPS, so the deal lifts our FY28E EPS by ~10%. But Gabriel holds minority stakes that partners (Dana, Henkel, HL) run, the promoter sat on both sides, and the profit share is not cash until paid as dividends.

arguments.h: Growth is real but the base is now harder to read
arguments.p: Q1FY27 revenue +15.5% (restated base), EBITDA +5%, PAT +2% as margins fell and the JV share rose 10%. FY24-25 are pre-scheme, FY26 is restated and FY27 holds the Jupiter stakes for part of the year, so like-for-like growth is hard to see. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|n1}}% in FY27E and EPS growth of ~25% in FY28E as HL Mando Anand counts for a full year.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair for the new Gabriel, rich for the old one
arguments.p: At ₹1,342 the stock trades at 36.4x our Sep-28E EPS and 59.2x trailing (restated, on today's shares), near its 38.1x post-scheme median but more than twice the ~15x it traded at on the old business's forward earnings in FY22-25. Brokers' post-Q1 targets (median ₹1,657) assume 32-40x on FY28E EPS of ₹35-41; on our EPS the same multiples give ₹1,100-1,375.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with HL Mando Anand, HL Klemove and the NCD interest; the first restated half-year balance sheet; whether commodity recoveries lift the standalone margin back above 9%.
Purchase-price allocation for the two new stakes (any amortisation of fair-value uplifts would cut the reported share of profit).
IGSS: PN3 approval for Inalfa to take 35% of the sunroof company (Gabriel to 65%).
Further group consolidation: ~30% of Anand Group businesses still sit outside Gabriel; any new related-party deal and its price.
Dana Inc. combining with Eaton's mobility business (announced Jun-2026): any effect on the Dana Anand JV.

sections.title: A ride-control maker that is becoming the Anand Group's listed holding company for auto parts

blocks.p: Gabriel India was set up in 1961 and is the flagship listed company of the Anand Group (promoter: Asia Investments Pvt Ltd, controlled by the Anand family). Its own business is ride control: shock absorbers, struts and front forks (500+ models) made in plants at Hosur, Nashik, Parwanoo, Sanand, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Chakan (two plants), Khandsa (Gurgaon) and Dewas (AR FY26), sold to two- and three-wheeler, car, truck and railway makers (88% of revenue) and through the aftermarket (12%). In FY26 two- and three-wheelers were ~62% of standalone sales, cars ~24%, trucks and railways ~13%. Since the scheme it also sells Anchemco's automotive fluids (diesel exhaust fluid, coolants, brake fluids), owns a sunroof maker (IGSS, with Inalfa of the Netherlands), 76% of a synchroniser-ring and aluminium-forging maker (ACYM) and 51% of a fastener start-up (with Jinhap of Korea). And it now holds minority stakes in five businesses run by foreign partners.

sections.title: Indian vehicle production is strong in 2026; ride control grows with it, not much faster

blocks.p: SIAM FY26 production: 2W +11.8% (scooters +17.2%, motorcycles +9.6%), 3W +23.9%, PV +9.4% (UVs +12.2%, cars +4.4%), CV +13.1% (M&HCV +16.1%, LCV +11.2%) (Q4FY26 deck slide 17). Q1FY27 production: 2W +23%, PV +17% (UVs +21%), CV +15% (call, 22-Jul-2026). The Sep-2025 GST cut on small cars and two-wheelers lifted demand from Q3FY26, so the FY27 comparison base rises from October. Shock absorbers are fitted to every vehicle (two on a scooter's rear or a fork at the front, four on a car, more on trucks), so volumes track production; value per vehicle rises with premiumisation (gas-charged and adjustable dampers, inverted forks on bigger motorcycles, SUVs taking a larger share of cars) and with new uses (cabin dampers on trucks, solar-tracker dampers, e-bike forks). Competitors include Munjal Showa, Endurance, ZF (Sachs), KYB, Tenneco and Mando itself.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Gabriel has a narrow moat: scale, approvals and decades of supply in a product every vehicle needs, strongest in trucks and electric two-wheelers. It has no pricing power. The stakes it has bought are better businesses (ROE 30-60% at Dana and Henkel), but Gabriel owns 25-49% of them, does not run them and depends on partners for technology. sections.title: Revenue 2.5x in five years on the old business; the scheme then added ~₹580 cr of revenue and ~₹180 cr of profit to FY26

blocks.p: Read the history in two parts. **The old Gabriel** (one ride-control company) grew revenue from ₹1,695 cr in FY21 (Covid) to ₹4,667 cr in FY26 as reported, ~22% a year, and lifted its EBITDA margin from 6% to ~9.5% as volumes recovered, two-wheelers premiumised and the sunroof subsidiary (from May-2023) and the Marelli Motherson suspension assets (Chakan-2, from Apr-2025) were added. Reported net profit rose from ₹60 cr to ₹252 cr. **The new Gabriel** is the FY26 the company restated in Jul-2026 for the scheme (pooling of interests): Anchemco's fluids and 76% of Anand CY Myutec add ~₹578 cr of revenue (to ₹5,245 cr), and the 25.1% of Dana Anand and 49% of Henkel Anand add ₹158 cr of equity-accounted profit. Restated profit to shareholders was ₹431 cr (reported ₹252 cr) and EPS ₹24.29 on the 17.72 cr post-scheme shares (₹17.55 reported). FY25 and earlier were not restated, so the FY26 step is not growth.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but restated, part-unreviewed history and a rising non-cash profit share

bullets: **Restated history.** FY26 was restated by pooling of interests; the undertaking's Q1FY26 and Q4FY26 figures were furnished by management and not reviewed by the auditor (results note 1). FY25 and earlier are not restated, Q2-Q3FY26 restated were not published separately, and FY27 will include the Jupiter stakes for ~6.5 months.

**Non-cash profit share.** Share of JV profit was 30.1% of restated FY26 profit before tax and ~46% of our FY28E. Cash arrives only through dividends set by the partners (none of the restated FY26 dividends are disclosed). The engine counts the share of profit as cash: our net cash forecast is therefore really "net cash plus the stakes at book".

**Fair-value stakes.** The Jupiter stakes were bought at negotiated values (₹2,231 cr and ~₹948 cr) and are carried as associates; the purchase-price allocation, and any amortisation of fair-value uplifts within the share of profit, was not known by 30-Sep-2026.
**Exceptional items.** FY26 had a ₹15.3 cr labour-code charge (consolidated). Deal advisory costs for Rise and Jupiter were expensed in the P&L and described as immaterial (CFO).
**Cash conversion of the operations is good.** Cash from operations was 73-97% of EBITDA in FY24-26 (Screener, pre-scheme); working capital is ~20-30 days.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unmodified PwC audit and a conventional business, but the reported numbers will be hard to compare for at least two years, a growing part of profit is a non-cash share of companies Gabriel does not control, and the inputs were set in related-party transactions.

sections.title: From net cash to ~₹1,250 cr of net debt: the balance sheet now holds ~₹3,600 cr of JV stakes

blocks.p: Before the deals Gabriel had almost no debt (₹148 cr incl. leases at Mar-26) and ₹324 cr of cash and investments. Our pro forma Mar-26 balance sheet adds the scheme (restated equity, ₹127 cr of Anchemco and ACYM debt, the Dana and Henkel stakes at ~₹395 cr) and Project Jupiter (₹2,231 cr HL Mando Anand stake, ₹948 cr HL Klemove stake, ₹1,000 cr NCDs, ₹237 cr deferred payment, ₹1,881 cr of new equity). Pro forma: net worth ~₹3,831 cr, borrowings ~₹1,512 cr (incl. the deferred payment), cash ~₹142 cr, other investments ₹121 cr and stakes ~₹3,574 cr. Net debt excluding the stakes is ~₹1,249 cr, ~2.5x FY26 EBITDA and ~1.6x FY26 EBITDA plus the pro forma JV share; CRISIL rates the NCDs AA+/Stable. Management spoke of debt/equity ~1:1; we get ~0.4x consolidated because the stakes were largely paid in shares. **Model note:** the engine and the Excel model read Screener's reported borrowings, fixed assets and working capital, so our model books the whole pro forma change against "Investments" (₹{{A.investments.7|num}} cr = stakes less the new net debt plus ~₹330 cr of the scheme's operating assets); net cash plus stakes is the same either way.

blocks.p: The scheme changed what a Gabriel share is: before Jul-2025 it was a single-product ride-control company trading at ~15x forward earnings; since the board approved the scheme (30-Jun-2025) the market has priced the restructured company, with stakes in group JVs. Like the Motherson and Aster DM initiations, we start the own-history window at that event. sections.title: Our honest summary: a good franchise wrapped in a group holding structure, fairly priced at 36.4x Sep-28E EPS; HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading shock-absorber maker (88% of trucks, ~60% of electric two-wheelers, a third of two-wheelers, a quarter of cars), a fluids business, a sunroof maker, and minority stakes in five group companies run by Dana, Henkel, SK, HL Mando and HL Klemove, three of them highly profitable. The Anand family owns ~66% and uses Gabriel to consolidate the group.

**What you are paying:** 49.1x our FY27E and 39.1x FY28E EPS. That is in line with the 38.1x the market has paid since the scheme was announced, but more than twice the ~15x it paid for the old Gabriel, at a time when auto-component peers trade ~9% below their own medians over the same period. ~46% of our FY28E profit before tax is a share of other companies' profit. dcf._betaWhy: Beta 1.0 (Ke 12.5%): cyclical auto volumes, but diversified across 2W, PV, CV and the aftermarket. Net debt (ex the JV stakes) is ~Rs1,200 cr, ~5% of enterprise value, so a WACC would be only slightly lower; the engine discounts at the cost of equity.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: India vehicle demand and content growth.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 3.5% of revenue in steady state (FY24-26 4-5%); depreciation 2.5%.
dcf._jvNote: FCFF excludes the JV share of profit; the JV stakes enter at book value through net cash (stake at cost plus accumulated share of profit), which understates Dana and Henkel (book ~Rs395 cr).
